sources.title: Jason's stoic character in Grand Theft Auto 6 was inspired by Steve McQueen and research into Army veterans: 'These guys typically aren't running their mouths'
sources.text: Rockstar made a point of creating "authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality." It's already clear that Grand Theft Auto 6 has a very different timbre than most other GTA games. While criminal hijinks and acerbic satire remain part of the experience, it's also much more interested in portraying characters and relationships in a more convincing, human fashion. One of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does. According to Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries, Jason's laconic nature was inspired by a personality type observed in both cinema and real-life. "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar ). Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." Humphries says this also "resonated" with research the studio was doing around Army veterans, particularly Army Rangers. In Grand Theft Auto 6 , Duval is a veteran of the game's equivalent military organisation called the Marauders. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries explained. Establishing a more grounded character was not solely a directive for Jason. It was a goal of the writing more broadly. This is interesting considering Florida was picked as the setting for GTA 6 in-part due to the wild 'Florida Man' stories that circulate on the Internet from the state. "Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe pointed out. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe continues. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What's important is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world." This is just one of the things that makes Rockstar's latest crime sim a marvel on pretty much all fronts . And while us PC gamers will have to wait an unspecified amount of time before it arrives on the platform, you can bet it going to be quite the experience when it does. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 has a 'complex drug network' that tracks everything from where drugs come from to 'how they eventually reach the street-level buyer'
sources.text: "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real." I've only dipped my toe into Grand Theft Auto 6 thus far, but I'm already impressed by the detail Rockstar has baked into its world. One thing I'm always curious about with games like this, however, is how much of that detail is on the surface versus what's actually happening under the hood. I'm still too early in the game to judge this for myself, but according to Rockstar, there is way more going on in terms of how NPCs behave than players will ever likely see. One striking example of this is how GTA 6 's gang compounds conduct their drug operations. In an interview with IGN , Rockstar's senior design director for its open world Steven Messinger explained that GTA 6 fully simulates drug distribution from top to bottom. "A big part of [the open world's design] was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories," Messinger pointed out. "For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we've fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they're distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer." Messinger notes that "players will only pick up bits and pieces of this". But representing this process wholesale means that, when players do notice it, it always feels authentic and believable. "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren't there." While this may only be designed for players to notice passively, I'm now keen to follow this system and see just how consistently it holds up. sources.title: GTA 6: Find and break into Freddie Gibbs’ doomsday compound in Grand Theft Auto 6
sources.text: How to find Freddie Gibbs, enter his compound, and get rewards in Grand Theft Auto 6 Rapper Freddie Gibbs is in Grand Theft Auto 6, and heâs a doomsday prepper with an impressive compound and bunker. Freddie is convinced that the apocalypse is coming, so heâs built up a doomsday bunker and compound, complete with an electric fence, mines, and even explosive drones. Thatâs just the defenses â heâs really prepared for the world to end. Freddie is a pretty nice and generous guy once you get to know him, but getting to know him isnât so easy. In this guide, weâre breaking down how to find and break into Freddieâs compound both times in GTA 6. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. Freddieâs compound is located on the North shore of Lake Leonida in North Leonard County. Itâs on the same road as One-Eyed Willieâs Auto Shop (Ultimate Edition exclusive). You canât miss it as itâs a large compound surrounded by electric fences, and has multiple billboards propped up warning about the end of the world. The first time you break into Freddieâs compound, it has an obvious flaw. A water tower to the rear of the compound is outside of the electric fence. It has an unblocked ladder that you can climb to take you up to a platform, from which you can jump onto the roof of a shed inside the electric fence. You will have to watch out for both proximity mines and drones. Proximity mines will be highlighted in Focus mode, and when you hear a drone, Focus mode will again give you enough time to shoot them down. The best route through the compound is sticking close to the fence while heading East, and then South. Proximity mines will not be placed on the pipes and cables in the compound, meaning you can use them as a walkway. You will complete the challenge by getting to the front door of the large dug-out bunker. The first time you complete this challenge, Freddie will free you and challenge you to return later, after he improves his defenses. After some time, Freddie will text Jason and Lucia, challenging them to a rematch. You need to break into his compound and get to the door of his bunker again, only this time the water tower isnât an option, and the proximity mines and drones have been buffed. Nothing is impossible, though, and Jason and Lucia are both pretty good climbers who are able to clamber on top of large vehicles. You see where this is going. To the rear of the compound â the Northwest corner â youâll find a tractor with a large trailer, along with a bulldozer. Park the tractor and trailer along the fence, and then use the bulldozer to lift the trailer into the air. This will give you the perfect ramp to climb up the tractor, onto the trailer, and over the electric fence. Even Freddie wonât see it coming. Head to the bunker door again with the same route as last time â while watching out for more mines â and Freddie will finally emerge to greet you before inviting you inside. A storm will start, and you will have to choose between staying or leaving. If you leave, Freddie will give you $6,250 cash. As a reward for staying with him, Freddie will give you the valuable Benefactor Dubsta that you can register and keep.

sources.title: GTA 6: Recover Jason’s stash from Key Lento in Grand Theft Auto 6
sources.text: How to recover Jason’s Key Lento Rainy-Day Fund stash in Grand Theft Auto 6 Mild spoiler alert: you should at least make it to Chapter 2 of Grand Theft Auto 6 before reading on. Things go very wrong at the climax of GTA 6âs first chapter. Jason and Lucia will have to abandon their home in Key Lento, and the stash of cash and Jasonâs collection of photographs go with them. But you can go back. The stash under the floorboards has burned up, but the money and photographs in the metal box are still intact, and you can recover them. Only, thatâs easier said than done. In this guide, weâre breaking down the best way to recover Jasonâs stash and photographs in Grand Theft Auto 6 . Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. To reiterate the above: the money you stashed under the floorboards will have burned up, but Jason did put $5,000 away as a Rainy-Day Fund for his family. If you stored more than that under the floorboards, Iâm sorry to say that the money is sadly gone. Still, the $5,000 is worth recovering, and thereâs at least one nice surprise to see. Your stash is, of course, in the same building that burned up in Key Lento. Cops will be patrolling the nearby area, and theyâll be stationed in front of Jasonâs house and on the dock around back, meaning you canât simply drive up in either a car or boat. The best option is to get a RydeMe taxi to a nearby location on the North or East side of the zone the cops are patrolling, like Chuckâs Tackle and Shot or The Rusty Anchor. Make sure to wear a disguise â hat, sunglasses, bandana â and sneak through gardens to get to the building North of Jasonâs burned-out home, just over the small canal where boats can dock. Cops wonât be patrolling this side of the house, meaning you can dive into the water and swim over to the boat ramp near Jasonâs basketball hoop. The stairs immediately in front of the ramp are very close to a pair of cops out front, so circle around the North side of the house and use the other stairs. If you stop to look under the stairs, youâll find Jasonâs snake Dolores has made a nest and laid some eggs. A happy ending. Climbing the stairs, youâll easily be able to find the stash and metal tin in the same place as ever. Quickly recover both the money and photographs, and escape the same way you came in before getting outside of the patrol zone and changing your disguise. Congratulations, youâve got some of your money back.

sources.title: Has Rockstar taken the "Grand Theft Auto" out of GTA 6? Or has it just gamified car-jacking properly for the first time?
sources.text: It's impossible to have a big game launch these days without some section of the internet, somewhere, finding grievances with the final product because it does not align with the expectations they had pre-release. The most recent upset comes in the form of Grand Theft Auto 6 's revised take on, well, grand theft auto. In case you're one of the few still unfamiliar, grand theft auto is more than the titular moniker for Rockstar's premier crime simulation series; it's actually a US legal term for the act of stealing or attempting to steal a motor vehicle. In most previous GTA entries, this was a central part of the core gameplay loop: accept a mission, nick a car, complete the mission, nick another car, getaway. It's an endemic part of the loop, and has become so popular and identifiable as such that even other games - Watch Dogs , Saint's Row, Cyberpunk 2077 , and so on - have emulated the mechanic. So it makes sense that the internet is in a bit of a spin about GTA 6's more mature and restrained take on its eponymous crime. A quick, no-frills getaway in a vehicle you've hijacked on the road isn't always the most effective option. A mindless crime spree on the streets of Leonida is not a simple thing to pull off, nor an easy thing to live down. In this game, actions have consequences, and an ill-timed or ill-judged car jacking can quickly and efficiently put an end to your criminal ambitions. That's not to say you cannot simply steal cars. Of course you can: the option to saunter up to an occupied vehicle and jack it from its registered owner is available to you from the very beginning of the game. But the citizens of Leonida aren't going to take your wanton act of foolishness lying down; many of the motorists in the county will fight back, pull a piece on you, or run you over mid-robbery attempt. Even if you are lucky to find one of the more pliant residents of the city, you might find something peculiar is happening in their car. I jacked a woman in the city over the weekend, and the cat she was ferrying from place to place decided to attack me, causing me to crash. I've heard other people say they've had muffled cries coming from the boot of the car where someone is transporting a hostage, or incidents where they've jacked the same person multiple times, leading to the poor car's owner to have a breakdown in the middle of the city. That cat event, the team here at Eurogamer has worked out, is an early game trigger - it seems stealing random cars early in the game will increase the chance of this encounter occurring. Rockstar's guiding hand is more visible here, then, in trying to teach you a lesson: don't steal cars. You're given your own - Jason's two-door coupé utility, a Vapid Creado - that I actually formed quite an emotional bond with in the opening 10-or-so hours of the game. 'Look after this car,' Rockstar insists, tutorialising you how to repair it, customise it, make it all pretty so it's in good condition when you go pick up Lucia for the first time. Shortly after the 10 hour marker, narrative events whisk you away elsewhere and you're given a 'slim jim', a long, thin tool that allows you to break into locked cars - something you could only do with a quick elbow jab before. The benefit here is two-fold; you can break into cars without setting off their alarms, and without breaking glass and lowering their resale value (something quite important in the earlier sections of the game). So, it takes you until Chapter 2 to start being able to more reliably and consistently break into vehicles. Good. And it'll take even longer to break into keyless vehicles. We're in 2026 after all, and it's heavily implied this is when GTA 6 is also set - it stands to reason that many cars run keyless fobs, and your old-school tools won't cut it if you want to break into a Zorruso, rather than an old Vapid truck. But then, even when you're well-armed and ready to start an illustrious new career as Vice City's most nefarious car thief, there's more to consider. Most modern cars also come with trackers: standard trackers simply prevent you modding cars you don't own (not an issue you'll face very often), but advanced trackers are more problematic. Boosting a car with an advanced tracker immediately alerts the cops to your location, and they close in on you fast . The only answer to this problem is flooring it, and outspeeding the signal ping the tracker is sending out: you need to drive fast and cleanly in order to stay mobile long enough for the tracker to deactivate, and this often incurs damage that makes selling these cars to fences a less viable option. You can't even sell cars with trackers installed at all to some fences until you're much, much further into the game. So, long story short, stealing cars is a faff in GTA 6. But I like that. I like that Rockstar has evolved the gameplay formula to more accurately reflect the state of the world in 2026. Modern problems require modern answers, and given that Rockstar has gone above and beyond in its creation of a sandbox simulation of Florida , I feel the immersion would be broken by just being able to saunter up to any car you want and break into it. No, needing a 'slim jim' or a key cloner - or needing to case my victims properly before trying to jack them - makes for a better game as far as I'm concerned. It makes me roleplay Jason and Lucia better, it makes me engage with the game's systems more, it makes me appreciate the cars that I do have whilst I have them. It also improves the flow of the game and how I interact with missions. I recently played GTA: Vice City , and after most missions were wrapped up, I would simply fling the nearest motorist onto the sidewalk, hop in their car, and drive away into the Malibu-styled sunset. I can't simply do that in GTA 6: I need to think about my getaway options, whether there's heat on my car, and where my next best (and cheapest) ride is going to be if a robbery or raid goes awry. sources.title: Why You Probably Shouldn't Steal a Tesla in GTA 6
sources.text: Since GTA 5 , Rockstar has parodied the Tesla brand with the fictional Coil line of cars. Well, with GTA 6 , Rockstar has taken the Tesla parody to another level. GTA 6 players have discovered that the game's version of Tesla cars are equipped with advanced security measures that prevent you from stealing the vehicle — and their owners get preferential treatment from the police. Whenever you try to steal a Coil car, a mechanism kicks in and locks you inside. Then, the car will either drive itself to the nearest police station, or force you to stay put until the cops arrive and arrest you. Do NOT steal is Tesla in GTA 6 😭 https://t.co/cYcsu7EWim GTA 6. 玩家不能偷老马的特斯拉 偷玩直接被自动驾驶送到警察局 太好玩了 #GTA6 #特斯拉 https://t.co/QvrQuvA2H7 Now, there is a way to escape, but you'll still be without the vehicle. It seems that the only way to make it out of there is to bust the window and climb out before the cops arrive. Otherwise, you can try and make a run for it when the cops drag you out of the car, but by that point you're probably surrounded and very much in tasering range. I hopped in-game to try this out, and found that none of the other Tesla-like electric vehicles produced the same results, so it's likely just the Coils that have this mechanic. You can't steal any of these electric cars until you get a key cloner anyway, but you can hop into one that's already unlocked (by 'borrowing' it from its owner when it's still running) and drive away to safety. They're worth a lot of money and are significantly cheaper to charge up as opposed to filling a car up with gas, so it's a good get if you can nab one. As for the Coils, you might have more luck if you find one where the security has been deactivated, but it's unclear if that's possible — if it is, we're all still looking for one. sources.title: Do You Need the Key Cloner to Steal All of GTA 6's Cars?
sources.text: Throughout your early hours in GTA 6, you may have been faced with many vehicles that you simply aren’t equipped to steal. It can be frustrating to walk up to a nice-looking car and be faced with the prospect of not being able to drive away in it because a “key cloner” is needed. Even if some oblivious rich person happens to leave their driver’s seat door open for you to slip into, you’ll still need the required tech to start the engine. Instead, you’ll have to wait until you can start cloning keys until you can experience the full range of Vice City vehicles available to you. Here’s when you’ll get it, and how it works. GTA 6 smartly staggers what class of car is available to you over the course of its story, minimising the risk that comes with jacking them as Jason and Lucia become smarter criminals. At first, you’ll be limited to rusty work vehicles and family sedans, but even these come with a risk. You’ll either have to steal them from somebody already driving, thus risking them alerting the cops to your crimes, or smash through a window to gain access, which is likely to raise an alarm. Your handy “Waink” scanner app on your phone can help you work out which vehicles you should be targeting. Those with the “key cloner” symbol attached to them are pointless to go after until partway through chapter three, which we’ll get onto soon. It’s not even until chapter two, and you meet Moses, that you’ll even be able to get into low-level cars easily. Upon working with Port Gellhorn’s mechanic, he’ll gift you a slim jim, meaning car window alarms no longer have to be triggered. Still, cars with digital keys and trackers inside them are still a no-go. In chapter three, Leonida’s full roster of vehicles will make themselves available to drive. You’ll get the key cloning device installed onto your phone during the appropriately titled “Clonin’ Keys, Makin’ G” mission, from Randy, a Vice City car shop owner. We have a detailed step-by-step guide on how to get the key cloner here . Randy acts similarly to Moses as a quest giver — asking you to recover specific cars with high sell-on values — but can cash in on ones with trackers built in. Once you’ve passed this main mission, you’ll now be able to fulfill your Grand Theft Auto fantasies and get behind the wheel of any Grotti, Pfister, or Pegassi that catches your eye. Just be aware that it won’t be simple to register these to either Jason or Lucia as personal vehicles straight away, though. Not only do they get quite expensive, but advanced trackers — GPS devices that track your location if you fall below a certain speed limit — can only be dealt with at Randy’s shop. Tick more and more cars off his desired checklist, though, and that may become a simpler process. So, in short, yes, you can steal every car in GTA 6; you just need to wait until chapter 3 in order to do so. There’s no getting the key cloner early, as it's tied to a main mission and can’t be found in the open world beforehand. Mattia may give you a taste of that supercar life early on during chapter one, but it's well worth the wait to get your hands on one for yourself. sources.title: How to steal the BF Bandito in GTA 6
sources.text: Track down this white off-roader for Moses. The BF Bandito is one of the many cars in GTA 6 that Moses asks you to steal and bring to him for cold, hard cash. This one has a search area out in Buskin Swamp, but when you arrive it's not immediately clear where or how to steal the car. The owner of this white offroad racer will drive around the map marked search area in a circle, as shown in the clip above. To get him to stop, simply park your car blocking the track and stand next to it. When he reaches you, he'll slow down and call out, at which point you should press L2 to focus on him and use the "Mislead" dialogue option to ask for help. In my version, Lucia was wearing a ski-mask and had a baseball bat, which quickly convinced them all to run away (after a few swings), but either way, once he stops it's easy to steal the car. The baseball bat probably wasn't necessary, but hey, it's still non-lethal. As you exit the swamp, you'll get shot at and pursued by a few of his friends, but the BF Bandito is fast enough to outrun them easily. Bring it back to Moses to get $3,400ish as reward, though this may vary based on condition. sources.title: How to get a key cloner in GTA 6
sources.text: The key cloner in Grand Theft Auto 6 allows you to steal keyless cars. As the most expensive cars in the game tend to be keyless, unlocking the key cloner is probably high on your priority list, but beware that it'll take a while to meet Randy, the key cloner expert. Here's where to find a key cloner in GTA 6 and how to use it. In GTA 6 's first chapter, you can only steal cars by smashing a window , which may set off an alarm. After meeting Moses in Chapter 2, you'll obtain a slim jim , which allows you to circumvent the alarm as you break in. Neither carjacking method, however, is enough to steal a keyless car. For that, you will need the key cloner . If you try to steal a keyless car before you've unlocked the key cloner, you can still break in, but you won't be able to drive away. It's therefore important to check the car's security system first; you don't want to smash a window and set off the car's alarm system, only to find that you can't use the car. To obtain the key cloner and steal keyless cars in GTA 6 , you must complete the following steps: To determine whether a car is keyless or not, use the WAiNK scanner on your phone (open the WAiNK app or hold the upward arrow on the D-pad for a shortcut). You'll see the words "key cloner" listed as the car's access type in the bottom right of your screen. To steal a keyless car in GTA 6 , interact with one of its front doors and select the "clone key" option (which appears instead of the "slim jim" option for non-keyless cars). Now, move the right stick in a circular motion until the center circle turns pink, and then hold the right stick in this position to unlock the car and drive off. Beware that most keyless cars are protected by a standard or advanced tracker . The standard tracker isn't much of a problem (it just means you can't modify the car unless you've registered it), but the advanced tracker, as you've experienced during "Steal the Zorrusso for Randy," is actively tracked by the police. The only way to stay ahead is to drive very fast. So, while you can steal both types with the key cloner, stealing cars with standard trackers is far easier. sources.text: Avengers: Doomsday is now just weeks away, and Marvel Studios continues to build hype with a new trailer for this year's highly anticipated Avengers sequel. The trailer offers the longest look yet at the movie, teasing several emotional hooks. We see Steve Rogers's life with Peggy and their young son, who was kept in the dark about Steve's past as Captain America. Perhaps most revealingly, we learn that Cap's decision to travel to the past has had unforeseen consequences when the Fantastic Four pay him a visit. Perhaps this is what Dr. Doom means when he refers to these characters living "stolen lives." The trailer ends with a callback to one of the Avengers series' best long-running bits as Cap asks Thor if the God of Thunder is bothered by the fact that Cap is holding his "former" hammer, Mjolnir. Additionally, we get more mutant action as Cyclops delivers the iconic "To me, my X-Men" line, summoning Nightcrawler along with Mystique and Gambit. If most of the film's teasers until now felt like they were mostly there to show off all the characters returning, this is the first one that felt like it offered a reason to care about this impending superpowered brawl. The latest trailer for Doomsday follows the first trailer released in July and an extended " special look " that emerged from Disney's D23 fan convention. After a series of middling box office showings for its superhero movies (Sony's Spider-Man: Brand New Day notwithstanding), Marvel Studios hopes to return to Avengers: Endgame -era glory with an all-star show of force that brings back characters from the past decade-plus of the MCU and the Fox era of X-Men films. Directors Joe and Anthony Russo return to Marvel with a mandate to revive the broad cultural interest (and box office) of their previous Avengers twofer. sources.title: Avengers: Doomsday final trailer has convinced me Steve Rogers got the bad ending in Endgame
sources.text: This is what it's like when worlds collide The Avengers: Doomsday final trailer is here, and it's all about Steve Rogers – from his personal sacrifice of leaving behind Peggy and their son, through to joining Thor and the OG X-Men in a battle against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. But the first minute or so of the trailer is riddled with inconsistencies about the one-time Captain America – and I think it's telling us more than it's letting on. The opening seconds of the Doomsday trailer again shows the moment Steve and Peggy reunite in Endgame. Then, it has a montage of a clean-shaven Steve packing away his Captain America gear, holding his baby boy, and later teaching him how to ride a bike. But the Steve we have seen so far – both in this trailer and elsewhere – shows him with longer hair and a beard, even right up to when the Fantastic Four rock up outside his doorstep. Apart from telling us that Doomsday picks up with Steve and Peggy having a teenage son sometime in the early 1960s, it appears that the Fantastic Four aren't crossing the multiverse to meet him. Instead, my theory is that Steve actually ended up visiting Peggy on Fantastic Four's Earth-828, a decision that caused much of the multiverse to collapse upon itself – and put Steve in Doom's sights. "We didn't know those choices would have consequences," Steve Rogers says of the decision to travel through time in Avengers: Endgame to reclaim the Infinity Stones and use them against Thanos in the Battle for Earth. Subscribe for a weekly digest of the movie and TV news that matters, direct to your inbox. From first-look trailers, interviews, reviews and explainers, we’ve got you covered. Simply put, Steve Rogers' past and present actions are catching up to him. He shouldn't have gone back through time (on either occasion), he is potentially on the wrong Earth, and he has a son that should never have existed. So, Avengers: Endgame's final dance could actually be the opening salvo to the universe ending – and caused the incursions (such as the worlds appearing in the sky in one Doomsday trailer moment) that is leading to the collapse of the universe. Good job, Steve. Avengers: Doomsday hits cinemas on December 14 in the UK and December 16 in the US. For more, we have a complete Avengers: Doomsday trailer breakdown for you to cast your eye over. sources.title: This '90s-inspired horror game has one of the coolest post-apocalyptic worlds I've ever seen
sources.text: Plus you can experience it all from the comfort of your campervan. I often find myself thinking where the best place to survive a zombie apocalypse would be. A walled-off stone house would certainly make for some good defenses, a boat would be great—but only if the zombies didn't pull a Fear the Walking Dead—or you could spend the end of the world in a camper van. That would certainly be whimsical. You do just this in The Road of Dust and Sorrow's demo , although it's certainly not as whimsical as I first imagined it to be. You see, in this 2D horror game you have bigger responsibilities than just keeping yourself alive, you also have a young daughter to look out for as well. This isn't an easy task. Supplies are dwindling, zombie-like humans infected by addictive chemicals amble across the land in search of more dust, but they'll settle for your blood instead. Plus there's this creepy Pastor who's definitely up to something very bad. I only got one glimpse of him in the demo and he was surrounded by a lot of gore and eldritch horror, so I've just decided that staying away from him is probably for the best. But you can't hunker down and forget about all these terrors, because you have a daughter to feed and protect. So I spent most of my time in the demo gathering food, medical supplies, and trying to locate an item that may just grant us safe passage to the only sanctuary humanity has left. The dev, Painted Black Games, says it took inspiration from horror series like Silent Hill and Resident Evil for The Road of Dust and Sorrow, and while I haven't come across anything particularly traumatic in a Silent Hill sense yet (although I wouldn't be surprised to see that here) I can see the through line to Resident Evil. The action is smooth, accurate, and rewarding—which surprised me as I usually don't vibe with 2D gunplay, sometimes the controls are too finicky, but it certainly works here. Head-shotting the zombies is incredibly satisfying, as is kicking them to the floor and beating them with a baseball bat. Then there are the puzzles. I didn't come across too many, but the ones I did find were very rewarding. It's not rocket science, but the solutions aren't always obvious either. They are, however, very intuitive; you can do a lot with a little, something I very much appreciate. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. But my favourite aspect of The Road of Dust and Sorrow has to be just how cool this post-apocalyptic world is. Maybe it's the pixel art, but it manages to look dilapidated and creepy while also being oddly pretty to look at. I was searching an abandoned warehouse full of zombies and rotting cargo while thinking to myself that with a bit of elbow grease this place could really scrub up. If you want pretty and cosy, though, the campervan is where it's at. I didn't spend as much time as I would have liked to there, but it managed to feel like a real home—the only safe place left in this world. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Elie is a news writer with an unhealthy love of horror games—even though their greatest fear is being chased. There’s no shortage of hard work involved in covering video games, but every so often you have one of those days that makes you stop and think: wow, I’m lucky to do this. This was one of them. For me, Rez was a revelatory experience that arrived during a formative moment in my life. I was about to turn 16, leave school, and enter a hedonistic life of clubbing, music, and the human connection that comes with it. At the same time, my gaming habits had broadened into a more eclectic mix of multiplatform games, with publications like Edge encouraging me to think more about them as an artistic medium. It was inevitable, then, that I’d eventually take a chance on an electric arthouse shooter from the arcade masters at Sega . I went in blind, and discovering its abstract wireframes and interactive techno beats for myself was a deeply affecting experience. It was like simultaneously conducting a Chemical Brothers album and the Ministry of Sound light show, behind the controls of a Space Harrier machine, in a combo only video games could power. To view Rez as simply a shooter is to completely miss its meaning. On the surface, it shares much with on-rails arcade games like Panzer Dragoon and Star Fox , tasking players with blasting their way through waves of enemies on route to a spectacular boss. But these familiar mechanics are a vehicle for something more transcendent. UGAâs young team were trying to do something few commercially developed games had attempted before. Rezâs central concept is synaesthesia, the phenomenon of one sensory experience triggering another, like sounds provoking certain shapes and colors. The player is treated as a participant in a performance, with the gameâs licensed music responding to every dispatched enemy with a hi-hat or synthesizer, like you’re some sort of Tron-age conductor. All the while, its pulsing, Kandinsky-inspired visuals move in harmony with the audio, and your game controller passes the vibrations through your body, as if youâve plugged the Dreamcast into your own auxiliary port. There was simply nothing else like Rez at the time. It isn’t hyperbole to say that United Game Artists’ extraordinary sensory alchemy fundamentally changed how I, and many others of a similar age, viewed video games and what they could be. Its sales werenât spectacular, but Rezâs cultural impact makes it as valuable as any blockbuster. “It isn’t hyperbole to say that United Game Artists’ extraordinary sensory alchemy fundamentally changed how I, and many others of a similar age, viewed video games and what they could be.” Rez mattered because it showed, at a time when creators were obsessed with emulating Hollywood, that video games could create experiences that other entertainment mediums couldnât replicate. With its Y2K-inspired aesthetic, arcade-coded design, and deep reverence for late 90s club culture, Rez is staunchly a creation of its time, but itâs also absolutely timeless. To this day, Iâll regularly throw some headphones on, or a VR headset, and blast through Area 3, with its thumping Ken Ishii techno, or if Iâm in a more energetic mood, the evolutionary rollercoaster of Adam Freelandâs finale, and go beyond synaesthesia. âI do think as time has marched on, the game has become more celebrated and dear to people than when it was originally released,â producer Tetsuya Mizuguchi tells me in a meeting room at his latest studio, Enhance (he wasnât the one driving the car, by the way â weâll get to that later). âWhen we were making it too, towards the end of development, it felt more like the start of something than the end of a project for me personally, but I didn’t really know what it was the start of. I think in many ways, because it was this primitive experience, because it didn’t fit exactly into one genre convention, perhaps one of the reasons it took some time for the adulation to come to the fore has a lot to do with it took people some time to find the words that allowed them to accurately describe what they liked about the experience.â It wasnât just the players who struggled to verbalize what that Rez experience meant, Mizuguchi says. âLooking back at myself and the development team, we had trouble when we were making it, trying to express what the team was and what we were after. âBack then, we’d spend a lot of time doing things like going to electronic music clubs and observing the crowds there, and the kind of different types of reactions they’d have as music would change, and what would move them, and trying to kind of pick up clues from that sort of reaction and human experience that we were trying to then apply into Rez. âBecause we were young, because we were fairly inexperienced, we were really operating a lot more off of intuition about what this game was going to become and how we were going to get there and what we were borrowing from these sort of observed human experiences. And so, in that sense, not just for the players, but for ourselves, it’s kind of taken these 25 years to better define what we were trying to go after and what made it special.â Mizuguchi describes the circumstances surrounding Rez’s development as something of a ‘perfect storm’, much of which was deliberately engineered. sources.title: Rockstar Says Jason's Viral Personality in GTA 6 Comes From Steve McQueen and Real-Life Veterans
sources.text: Rockstar Games has opened up about GTA 6 protagonist Jason's viral personality and the two specific inspirations that helped bring him to life. As 13 years of waiting for the next Grand Theft Auto ended last week, players have found themselves enamored with Jason Duval. Stoic, nonchalant, calm, composed, resigned; whatever you want to call one of GTA 6's new protagonists, Rockstar says it carefully crafted his already iconic demeanor by pulling from a Steve McQueen classic and real-life veterans. The studio's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, talked about how the studio behind the mega-hit video game built Jason from the ground up during a conversation with Destructoid . Centering the story on a "couple on the run" marked new territory for Rockstar, but it's far from a new concept in entertainment. So, the team turned to movies, particularly Sam Peckinpah's The Getaway. "Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone," Humphries explained. "We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." He continued, saying that Rockstar's research into real-world veterans and Army Rangers helped refine its approach. Those who have played the game (and keen-eyed trailer watchers ) already know about Jason's military background, so the influence here definitely tracks. "These guys typically aren’t running their mouths or reacting to something unless it’s strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves." Jason is the talk of Vice City and has been for some time. As Rockstar shared more details about its seemingly shy lead ahead of GTA 6's launch, some fans began to wonder if he could be the franchise's first-ever neurodivergent protagonist . In addition to his personality, Humphries described Jason as "wired differently" during a recent interview with Love magazine. While Jason steals more than just wads of cash in Vice City, his partner in crime has proven to be just as impactful. Game writer Michael Wiafe said looking into the kind of criminal activity known to make headlines in Florida was one of the first things the team did when creating both Jason and Lucia. For Rockstar, it wasn't just about creating true-to-life criminals; it was about creating fully realized human beings. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn’t stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe said. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What’s important is how they resonate, no matter where you’re experiencing the game in the world." Between the chaos of robbing gas stations and drug dealers and getting into high-speed car chases, Jason and Lucia can become quite the power couple. Game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern said to Destructoid, "You really want them to make it." The quiet moments where the duo scrolls through social media in their bed or drives the other one to work can be just as important as the action set pieces. Gauvey-Kern added, "Those need to hit too, and you need to connect with how the characters are feeling in those moments." Although GTA 6 launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S three days ago, Leonida is packed with enough things to do to keep players playing for months. While we wait to see what's next for Rockstar, you can check out IGN's 10/10 review . You can also read about how the developers made every NPC feel like real people you could run into on the street . Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

sources.title: GTA 6's strong and silent Jason was inspired by Steve McQueen and former Army Rangers, says Rockstar
sources.text: If you've noticed that Grand Theft Auto 6's Jason Duval isn't much of a talker, that's by design, as his quiet nature was inspired by Steve McQueen and the studio's research into former Army Rangers. Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story. "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was Peckinpah's The Getaway ," Humphries said. "Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." That approach also fitted the studio's research into veterans. "This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders)," Humphries continued. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves." Game writer Michael Wiafe said Florida's real-life crime stories were "an obvious starting point" for GTA 6's characters more broadly. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe said. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them." Fellow writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern added that while "the story takes some pretty heavy turns", Jason and Lucia's goal remains consistent. "So sharing their sense of determination, the focus on their goal, through all the highs and lows - that's what I hope people feel more than anything. You really want them to make it." GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day , not everyone is happy: some players have been review bombing its Metacritic user score over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda. Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review . If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats . Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort .

sources.title: GTA 6 "girlfriend simulator" complaints "are real" at first, ex-Rockstar lead says
sources.text: Obbe Vermeij says he's "having loads of fun now" he's further into the game One former Rockstar Games lead has a revolutionary take about GTA 6 – "it is good." But even though that may be the case, he reckons that "the complaints are real" in Chapter 1 from those suggesting that it "doesn't feel like a sandbox" and instead feels like a "girlfriend simulator." Obbe Vermeij worked at Rockstar Games between 1995 and 2009, serving as technical director on GTA 3, 4, Vice City, and San Andreas. Obviously, he'd left the studio well before GTA 6 started development (it might have been a long time coming, but it wasn't that long), so he's been playing through it alongside the rest of us. "It is good. Very good," he begins in a post on Twitter . However, there's a "but" coming. "In chapter 1 (The first 8 hours or so) the game doesn't give you much choice," he continues. "There are many tutorials, cut scenes, mandatory missions and the missions are basic. The complaints are real (realism over gameplay, girlfriend simulator, doesn't feel like a sandbox)." Opinions here do vary – I've definitely seen more than a few social media posts complaining about the optional tasks of grocery shopping for Lucia and buying her flowers, for example. They probably weren't high up the list of activities fans who planned to enter Leonida and immediately commit heinous crimes had in mind, I suppose – though it's worth keeping in mind that, again, those parts are optional. Equally, though, I've seen plenty of people enjoying the almost life-sim-esque vibe of GTA 6's opening hours, and that's probably reflected in how much time people spend in that first chapter. As someone who spent 18 hours in Chapter 1, you can probably guess what camp I fall into. Regardless, though, Vermeij reckons things really pick up by the time you reach the second chapter. "In chapter 2, the game backs off and gives you a bunch of missions to choose from," he says. "This is when the GTA magic kicks in." Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Vermeij says he's now 46% of the way through the story in Chapter 3 and "having loads of fun now." He concludes that the "production values are unreal," and I don't think anyone could disagree with that. GTA 6 review s have been glowing across the board, and Rockstar has already achieved almost unfathomable commercial success, with a whopping 32.5 million copies sold via pre-orders (eclipsing a figure that took Elden Ring three years to reach) and earning $3.79 billion on day one. It had the biggest entertainment launch in history – I don't think the devs could have hoped for anything better. sources.text: Domingo é dia da nossa lista de lançamentos de jogos, para que você possa programar a sua agenda nos próximos dias. E o destaque dessa vez é Arkheron , game desenvolvido por um dos criadores de World of Warcraft e que mistura elementos de ação em tempo real com estratégia e coleta de itens ao longo das fases. Outro destaque é Appulse. O game conta com uma proposta ousada de misturar elementos de ação em tempo real, mais precisamente no controle de naves, a uma espécie de mesa de pinball interativa. Confira a lista completa de lançamentos da semana e os respectivos preços. Athelan Battlegrounds é um jogo de estratégia tática por turnos desenvolvido por uma equipe independente de duas pessoas. A proposta mistura elementos de xadrez com mecânicas de jogos competitivos em arenas, colocando os jogadores para montar equipes e disputar partidas estratégicas contra outros oponentes online. O título aposta em um sistema competitivo baseado apenas na habilidade dos participantes , sem mecânicas de progressão que ofereçam vantagens fora das partidas ou recursos pagos que influenciem o resultado. O game será distribuído de forma gratuita no PC através do Steam e já conta com uma versão demo para download. Appulse é um jogo de tiro com visão superior inspirado nas mecânicas clássicas de pinball. Ambientado no espaço, você precisa assumir o controle de uma nave e, assim, dominar o recuo das armas para controlar a trajetória da esfera pelo tabuleiro enquanto protege sua nave-mãe contra ondas de robôs invasores. A cada nível alcançado, é possível escolher melhorias para personalizar o arsenal, as habilidades e os recursos da mesa , além de utilizar um canhão de ejeção para invadir naves inimigas e cumprir objetivos específicos. O jogo ainda não possui um preço definido, mas já conta com uma versão demo disponível de forma gratuita. Arkheron é um jogo de ação isométrico focado em partidas competitivas entre equipes. A dinâmica consiste em escalar uma torre ao lado de dois aliados, enfrentando outros grupos de jogadores e coletando equipamentos pelo caminho que alteram as habilidades e a forma de jogar no meio dos combates. O título, que foi desenvolvido pelo veterano de World of Warcraft , Rob Pardo, também contará com um visual repleto de detalhes, além de um sistema de ranqueamento para possíveis torneios no futuro. O jogo ainda não possui um preço definido, mas é possível se inscrever para o período de testes, que ainda está em andamento. E na sua opinião, qual o game mais esperado da semana?
